title: The earliest tournament on record ran in a Stanford computer lab in 1972
description:
The earliest tournament on record ran in a Stanford computer lab in 1972 The Intergalactic Spacewar Olympics, organised by Rolling Stone writer Stewart Brand, took place on the evening of 19 October 1972 at Stanford's Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, with roughly twenty competitors.

A Stanford graduate student who won the five-player free-for-all, practising left-handed and two-fisted play against beginners just to keep his own games interesting.

A year of Rolling Stone magazine, and by one attendee's account, some beer Stewart Brand organised the tournament and covered it himself for a Rolling Stone feature, 'Fanatic Life and Symbolic Death Among the Computer Bums', published 7 December 1972.

The photographer covering it that night, Annie Leibovitz, would go on to take John Lennon's last professional photograph and portrait Queen Elizabeth II.
